subject: FlightDeck dedicated capacity: absorption playbook & headroom ask
messages:
From: Alex Tanner <alex@flightdeck.ai>
To: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@flightdeck.ai>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@flightdeck.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing question — FlightDeck production profile

Hi David / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a short internal exercise and wanted to share a conservative expected production profile so you can recommend sizing for a Dedicated pool. Attached is a CSV with anonymized traces (sampled 2 weeks). Quick summary: 

- Peak sustained TPS (tokens/sec across all users): ~18k tokens/s
- 95th-percentile request size: ~1.4k tokens (avg ~420 tokens)
- Burst cadence: short spikes (~15–60s) roughly 4x baseline arriving from scheduled jobs

Our SLO target: 95th latency under 450ms for text-generation p95 (same model family as your m-family medium). We also need an operational headroom buffer for unexpected growth in month 1.

Can you propose slab sizing and a short runbook for absorbing bursts? We want a recommendation we can review with procurement this week.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Tanner
Head of Engineering, FlightDeck
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tanner <alex@flightdeck.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question — FlightDeck production profile

Alex — thanks for the trace and the clear SLO. I pulled the CSV and ran it through our quick-sizing heuristic (model perf profile + token distribution). High-level recommendation below; see details and caveats after.

Summary recommendation (initial committed slab):
- Baseline slab: 8 Dedicated GPUs (A100/80GB equiv) reserved — supports sustained ~20k tokens/s with p95 headroom margin at current request mix.
- Burst buffer: +3 GPU burst capacity (on reserved-burst tier) to cover short 4x spikes — auto-burst with warm KV-cache routing.
- Canary / rollout: Start with 4 GPUs in a canary pool serving 20% traffic for 48 hours before full cutover.

Why this maps to your SLO:
- Our internal perf numbers for the m-family medium under continuous batching match ~2.4k tokens/s per GPU at p95 for 1.4k-token requests when prefix KV hits are common. That yields ~19.2k tokens/s on 8 GPUs with typical batching.
- The +3 GPUs give ~9k tokens/s burst capacity; with our routing policy we expect to absorb 60–80% of short spikes without degrading p95 beyond 450ms.

Operational notes / runbook (short):
1) Warmup: Pre-warm KV caches for scheduled job windows — execute a lightweight prefetch 10min before known spikes.
2) Throttles: Apply soft token throttling for uncontrollable backfills — prefer 429 with Retry-After for long-running jobs.
3) Fallbacks: Configure automatic model-variant fallback (medium -> small quantized) for non-critical routes when p95 > 600ms for >2m.
4) Observability: Add a short eval set (50 queries) tracked each minute to detect quality regressions during canary.

Caveats: we assumed your traces include similar KV-cache locality to the sample; if your effective context hit rate is <40% throughput per GPU drops ~20%. Also scheduling jitter can make bursts longer than the 60s sample; if that occurs we should reserve an extra GPU.

I'll attach the quick calc and a sample token-to-GPU mapping in the follow-up. Kimberly — can you propose commercial commit tiers that match 8+3 (reserved + burst) and the terms for canary? Priyom / Marissa — tagging you for any infra or perf constraints we should dial back before proposing to procurement.

— David
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tanner <alex@flightdeck.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@flightdeck.ai>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial — Draft commit proposal for FlightDeck (8+3 burst)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Following David's sizing, attaching a draft commercial outline for the 8 GPU reserved slab plus 3 GPU burst buffer. Key commercial points:

- Commit: Monthly reserved fee for 8 GPUs; burst credits billed as hourly usage at discounted burst rate.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on reserved capacity; p95 latency target documented in the SLO appendix.
- Canary: 2-week commercial waiver on overage fees for canary (first 48h technical canary, then 2 weeks observation).
- Term options: 12/24/36 months with stepped discounts — standard is 12m.

Next steps: if flightdeck is comfortable with 8+3 we can issue an MSA draft and schedule a short procurement call (Emily included).

Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Tanner <alex@flightdeck.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@flightdeck.ai>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@flightdeck.ai>
Date: 2026-07-21T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question — FlightDeck production profile

Thanks team — this is very helpful and pragmatic. A few quick clarifications before procurement: 

- Could you add a sensitivity table showing required GPUs if our 95% context hit rate drops to 25% (we have some batch jobs that bypass cache)?
- For the canary, we prefer a single 72-hour technical canary (20% traffic) followed by a commercial observation period. Can you confirm instrumentation requirements (which metrics / dashboards you'll add)?

We'll review the draft MSA once received. Attaching the sampled CSV and a short procurement checklist for your reference.

Next call: can we lock 30 minutes Thu morning to run the sensitivity table and procurement checklist?

— Alex
Alex Tanner
Head of Engineering, FlightDeck
